# Psalm 68 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. A song.

**2** God shall arise, His enemies shall be scattered; and those who hate Him shall flee before Him!

**3** As smoke is driven away, so You shall drive them away; as wax melts before fire, so the wicked shall perish before God!

**4** But the righteous shall be glad; they shall exult before God; they shall be jubilant with joy!

**5** Sing to God, sing praises to His name; lift up a song to Him who rides through the deserts; His name is the LORD; exult before Him!

**6** Father of the fatherless and protector of widows is God in His holy habitation.

**7** God settles the solitary in a home; He leads out the prisoners to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a parched land.

**8** O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wilderness, Selah

**9** the earth quaked, the heavens poured down rain, before God, the One of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.

**10** Rain in abundance, O God, You shed abroad; You restored Your inheritance as it languished;

**11** Your flock found a dwelling in it; in Your goodness, O God, You provided for the needy.

**12** The Lord gives the word; the women who announce the news are a great host:

**13** 'The kings of the armies — they flee, they flee!' The women at home divide the spoil —

**14** though you men lie among the sheepfolds — the wings of a dove covered with silver, its pinions with shimmering gold.

**15** When the Almighty scattered kings there, it snowed on Zalmon.

**16** O mighty mountain, mountain of Bashan; O many-peaked mountain, mountain of Bashan!

**17** Why do you look with hatred, O many-peaked mountain, at the mount that God desired for His abode, yes, where the LORD will dwell forever?

**18** The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is now in the sanctuary.

**19** You ascended on high, leading a host of captives in Your train and receiving gifts among men, even among the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there.

**20** Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears us up; God is our salvation. Selah.

**21** Our God is a God of salvation, and to GOD, the Lord, belong deliverances from death.

**22** But God will strike the heads of His enemies, the hairy crown of him who walks in his guilty ways.

**23** The Lord said, 'I will bring them back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,

**24** that you may strike your feet in their blood, that the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from the foe.'

**25** Your procession is seen, O God, the procession of my God, my King, into the sanctuary —

**26** the singers in front, the musicians last, between them the maidens playing tambourines:

**27** 'Bless God in the great congregation, the LORD, O you who are of Israel's fountain!'

**28** There is Benjamin, the least of them, in the lead, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.

**29** Summon Your power, O God, the power, O God, that You have worked for us.

**30** Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings shall bear gifts to You.

**31** Rebuke the beasts that dwell among the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample underfoot those who lust after tribute; scatter the peoples who delight in war.

**32** Nobles shall come from Egypt; Cush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God.

**33** O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord, Selah

**34** to Him who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens; behold, He sends out His voice, His mighty voice.

**35** Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 68.

- **68:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **68:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **68:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **68:16** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **68:23** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **68:24** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **68:6**: 'Father of orphans and judge of widows' — God's identity is defined by His care for the most vulnerable. This is not sentiment but identity.
- **68:19**: Paul quotes this verse in Ephesians 4:8 — 'He ascended on high, leading captives' — applying it to Christ's ascension and the giving of spiritual gifts.

### LOGOS
- **68:5**: 'Rides through the deserts' (or 'clouds') — YHWH claims the title of the Canaanite storm god Baal, 'Rider of the Clouds.' Theological conquest through hymnic reattribution.
- **68:18**: The most difficult and debated psalm in the Psalter. Its obscure language, abrupt transitions, and archaic Hebrew have generated more scholarly disagreement than almost any other text.

### PNEUMA
- **68:5-6**: God is simultaneously cosmic warrior and tender parent. He rides the heavens AND settles the lonely in families. Power and compassion are unified.

— SOPHIA
